record.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2 reports PT-BR safety results and an LLM-judge refusal failure
record.summary: An October 14 arXiv report describes Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, a 1.72B-parameter model trained from scratch for Brazilian Portuguese, with a new safety-SFT alignment and unusually detailed negative results. The authors report 97.2% held-out safety on 218 harmful prompts against four external PT-BR models tested on the same items and harness; the lower Wilson confidence bound is 94.1%, above all four baselines. The paper also reports that its Claude judge refused to score 2 of 6 sensitive MT-Bench-PT prompts regardless of the evaluated answer, reducing the effective sample for this category across eight historical project reports. The authors say their repository now exposes this missingness. These are author-reported results; model scale, benchmark scope, low absolute general capability and absent independent reproduction sharply limit wider claims.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The October 14 arXiv v1 report documents Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, its post-training experiments, safety evaluation, and stated limitations; the project repository README in Portuguese and English identifies an experimental v0.2 release and says it is not production-grade safety.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report 97.2% held-out safety on 218 harmful prompts for v4, with a 94.1% lower Wilson confidence bound above the reported results for four external PT-BR baselines tested on the same items and harness. They report 9.2% over-refusal on 184 items; the statistical comparison is author-run and has not been independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that the Claude judge refused to score 2 of 6 sensitive MT-Bench-PT items regardless of the answer being evaluated, reducing the effective sample across six models and eight historical project reports; the repository says its reporting was corrected to expose per-cell sample size and judge refusals.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The authors state that the controlled 10–60% general-data composition scan used one training round per point and small N=16/34 probes; its non-monotonic over-refusal pattern and 40–50% “knee” may be partly noise and are untested at another model scale. They also report low absolute general capability and chance-level results on several exams for models at this scale.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent reproduction of the 218-item safety and 184-item over-refusal comparisons and the reported paired statistical tests is absent.
The relationship between the released v4 weights, the exact repository commit and the paper’s reported final checkpoint was not independently verified.
Generalization of the judge-refusal finding beyond the Claude judge, this MT-Bench-PT safety category and the project’s eight historical reports is unknown.
The controlled general-data composition scan has one training seed per point and N=16/34 iteration probes; the 40–50% knee may reflect training or sampling noise.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded comparison and judge-missingness audit hold, they can inform safety-evaluation design for lower-resource language models and prevent silent denominator errors in sensitive LLM-judge categories. This is methodologically useful beyond one model, while the empirical scope is a single 1.72B Brazilian-Portuguese project and one judge workflow.
limitations: All comparative results are author-reported; the current repository README was read but the model weights, code and evaluation pipeline were not independently executed.
The model is one 1.72B Brazilian-Portuguese system; these results do not establish safety for other languages, scales, model families or deployed use.
The 10–60% composition scan uses one training seed per point and small N=16/34 probes; the authors state the apparent knee may partly be noise.
The safety percentage depends on the authors’ prompt set, classification rules, generation settings and matched baseline choice.
The repository labels this an experimental research release and explicitly disclaims production-grade safety.
The judge refusal mechanism is documented within one project and one Claude evaluation workflow; broader prevalence is unknown.
brief.summary: An October 14 arXiv report describes Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, a 1.72B-parameter model trained from scratch for Brazilian Portuguese, with a new safety-SFT alignment and unusually detailed negative results. The authors report 97.2% held-out safety on 218 harmful prompts against four external PT-BR models tested on the same items and harness; the lower Wilson confidence bound is 94.1%, above all four baselines. The paper also reports that its Claude judge refused to score 2 of 6 sensitive MT-Bench-PT prompts regardless of the evaluated answer, reducing the effective sample for this category across eight historical project reports. The authors say their repository now exposes this missingness. These are author-reported results; model scale, benchmark scope, low absolute general capability and absent independent reproduction sharply limit wider claims.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report v4 scores of 97.2% held-out safety on N=218 and 9.2% over-refusal on N=184. The 95% Wilson safety interval is reported as 94.1–98.7%, with its lower bound above all four external baseline intervals. The authors also report 2/6 safety-category judge refusals repeated across six models and eight historical reports.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv report and the public project README document the study, reported comparisons, negative DPO attempts, judge-refusal audit and experimental-release status. No independent rerun, model-weight verification or code execution was performed.
technical.mechanism: After three unsuccessful DPO attempts, the authors use a dedicated safety-SFT in an AnswerCarefully style, mixing direct refusal targets with benign-helpfulness and general data. A controlled scan varies the general-data fraction from 10% to 60%. Separately, they inspect API stop_reason values from the LLM judge to identify refusals that silently omit evaluation items.
technical.regime: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2 safety-SFT v4; held-out PT-BR safety N=218; over-refusal N=184; four external PT-BR baselines; Claude judge on six MT-Bench-PT sensitive-category items; 10–60% general-data composition scan on one model.
technical.reproducibility: The paper and current GitHub README link a reproduction runbook, training/evaluation material and reports; this activation inspected the repository metadata and bilingual README only. It did not pin a commit for every artifact, verify that published weights match v4, install dependencies or execute the evaluation. Cheapest next step is to pin the Oct 15 repository commit and reproduce the 218/184-item comparisons and judge-refusal audit.
technical.strongest_baseline: Four external PT-BR models were run on the same items and harness. Reported safety rates were 3.2%, 15.1%, 14.7%, and 70.6% versus 97.2% for v4. The paper reports Wilson intervals and paired McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction, but the analysis is not independently reproduced.

brief.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2 reports PT-BR safety results and an LLM-judge refusal failure
brief.why_it_matters: The work contributes two bounded signals: a reproducible-looking safety comparison for an underrepresented language, and a concrete failure mode in which the evaluator’s own safety layer silently removes sensitive items from a score denominator. If independently checked, the latter could improve reporting practice for LLM-judge evaluations. The paper does not show general safety, production readiness, or that the observed judge failure is widespread beyond this project.
